InterGroup Consultants Ltd. (in association with PROLOG Canada) (2017). Natural Gas as a Fuel for Mine Haul Trucks. Final Report, NRCan Contract #3000631963, submitted to Natural Resources Canada, Ottawa, 30 March 2017.

Loaded: diesel haul-truck fuel use per operating hour, payload and utilization for six payload classes (Table 2-3 study assumptions) with GJ/h derived at the report factor 0.0368 GJ/L; diesel litres per kt material removed across nine Canadian open-pit mines (reprinted from NRCan 2005); Casino Mine 360 t and 90 t truck fuel rates; diesel and LNG CO2e factors; LNG dual-fuel conversion kit capex (150-300k per truck), oil sands case-study implied conversion+refueling cost, HPDI added cost (~600k); GHG reduction percentages (Scenario 1 13%, Scenario 2 25%; Table 3-1 literature values). Other-values: fleet counts and diesel volumes, scenario totals, displacement rates, fuel-price gaps. Not loaded: Table 4-1/4-3 fuel cost savings (price-scenario outputs), air pollutant reductions (non-GHG), LNG supply-chain prices (Fig. 2-2), Casino mine capital totals. Locator: printed section-page numbers (e.g. p.2-7 = PDF page 21). Traps: (1) per-hour fuel rates are study assumptions, not measurements; (2) currency and price year of conversion costs not stated - CAD and 2017 assumed (scenarios state 2016$); (3) the report prints 0.0368 GJ/L in Sect. 1.3 but 0.03868 GJ/L in fn 94 (NEB 38.68 GJ/m3) - Table 4-1 TJ values confirm 0.03868 (168.1 ML -> 6,501 TJ), so 0.03868 used for derived GJ/h; (4) LNG emission factor excludes methane slip; (5) the per-truck service unit does not match the t-based haul-truck archetype except for the L/kt range.
